guidance: A reading-order and bar-count model, not playback: it assumes the sections are listed in printed order and does not model pickup bars, fermatas, tempo changes, nested voltas or a repeat that closes inside a jump target.
method: Each section is listed once in printed order with its written bar count and the number of times its repeat is taken, from 1 to 8. The first pass plays the sections in order and expands every written repeat. With an al Coda roadmap the first pass stops before the Coda block, which is the Coda section together with every section after it, so the Coda is entered only from the repeat pass. A D.C. roadmap then returns to the first section and a D.S. roadmap to the named Segno, and the jump pass plays forward to the Fine section inclusive or to the To Coda section inclusive; an al Coda roadmap then continues from the Coda section to the end. Written repeats are played again on the jump pass only when that option is ticked, because scores commonly drop them after a D.C. or D.S.; otherwise each section on the jump pass sounds once. Fine ends the jump pass, To Coda must sit at or after the jump point, and the Coda must follow the To Coda section. Section names are trimmed, limited to 24 characters and unique ignoring case, bars are whole numbers from 1 to 999, repeats are whole numbers from 1 to 8, and there are between 1 and 24 sections. Bar numbers count performed bars from the first played bar, not printed bar numbers. Pickup bars, fermatas, tempo changes, nested or partial volta brackets, and repeats that close inside a jump target are not modelled: the result is a reading order and a bar count, not playback or a time estimate. Everything is calculated in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Da capo: D.C. returns to the beginning; al Fine stops at the word Fine, and al Coda repeats from the beginning until the first coda sign and then skips to the coda
Wikipedia, Dal segno: D.S. returns to the segno, al fine plays until Fine, al coda leaves at To Coda for the coda, and a fine or coda sign is ignored until a later D.S. instructs the player to use it
Wikipedia, Repeat sign: repeat barlines enclose the passage to be played twice, and first and second endings choose a different close on each pass
